strengths: Well-motivated observation that offline SFT performance does not translate to post-RL performance; Figure 1 convincingly demonstrates offline-online ranking reversals
Sound application of off-policy evaluation theory to correct behavior-target policy mismatch, with clear connection to importance sampling
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 6 model families and multiple benchmarks with substantial empirical gains (14.6% Pass@8 on AIME-2025, 40% absolute accuracy on logic games)
Practical method that works as a plug-in reweighting approach with both NLL and KL objectives, applicable to different model sizes
Thorough analysis including gradient alignment (Figure 7), parameter drift (Figure 8), and transfer to different task distributions (Table 4)
Clear presentation of motivation, method variants, and algorithm; Figure 2 provides excellent intuition
weaknesses: Limited novelty: applies well-established OPE techniques to a new problem; concurrent works (iw-SFT, DFT, AwSFT, Proximal-SFT) propose similar importance-weighting schemes but are not experimentally compared, only citing a generic 'Single Step IS' baseline
Scope restricted to verifiable reasoning tasks with deterministic correctness labels; generalizability to open-ended generation, knowledge tasks, or other capabilities is unclear and untested

Critical experimental gaps: Figure 1 lacks error bars/confidence intervals despite RL variance; missing ablations on hyperparameters (γ=0.999, clipping bounds, block size B); no seed averaging reported; unclear if ranking reversals are statistically significant

Incomplete description of design choices: negative example selection (§3.6, §4.5) underdocumented; offline data generated from Qwen3-8B makes it unclear whether improvements come from PEAR or stronger baseline data

Theoretical gaps: no formal analysis of why this reweighting leads to better RL initialization; connection between suffix ratios and Q-values (Appendix C) is intuitive but hand-wavy; offline data generation mechanism (behavior policy specification) may not hold in practice

Methodological concerns: Table 4 shows dramatic performance variation across task distributions (2.8%→38.3% for 1.7B), suggesting potential fragility; analysis findings somewhat tautological (RQ1) or modest (RQ2 gradient angle 51.27°→52.53°); causality between NSS and RL performance unclear
Missing comparisons to closely related concurrent work despite citing 6+ similar methods; no evaluation on other RL algorithms beyond GRPO or other capability domains
